name: Marginal Intelligence Budget
purpose: Use contributed Intelligence Fund money only where paid capacity measurably improves Brain Trust answer quality, reliability, verification or synthesis beyond the zero-price baseline.
principles: Run capable zero-price or local models first when they are adequate.
Never pay merely to display more AI names or duplicate an answer.
Prefer paid calls that correct, verify, add a genuinely different useful angle, or produce a substantially better final synthesis.
Never silently substitute one provider's output for another provider's identity.
Show outages, quota limits and unavailable providers rather than hiding them behind fake participation.
Re-check current provider pricing before changing paid routing because model prices and promotions change.

routingStrategy.tier0: Free/local first: answer, classify the problem, and identify whether another model is likely to add value.
routingStrategy.tier1: Micro-checker: use a low-cost model for a short independent correction, missing-angle or factual-risk pass instead of asking it to rewrite the entire answer.
routingStrategy.tier2: Specialist: spend on a model whose capability matches the task only when the baseline has a gap, material disagreement, tool need, or repeated failure.
routingStrategy.tier3: Premium judge: one strong model adjudicates unresolved disagreements or performs the final synthesis; do not call every premium model by default.
routingStrategy.stopRule: Stop buying additional opinions when the estimated probability of a useful new contribution multiplied by its value is lower than the expected call cost or when two consecutive independent checks add no material information.

efficiencyTactics: Send expensive models a compact claim-and-disagreement summary instead of the entire raw transcript whenever full context is unnecessary.
Cap checker outputs tightly; verification normally needs a delta, not another essay.
Cache identical or near-identical verification work when the underlying facts and freshness requirements have not changed.
Use task-aware routing: cheap fast models for classification and sanity checks, stronger models for hard synthesis and adjudication.
Prefer providers with proven low truncation and retry rates even when their nominal token price is slightly higher.
Benchmark a new paid route with a small canary budget before granting it a larger share.
For non-urgent work, use discounted batch or off-peak capacity when a provider offers it and the user has opted into economy mode.

measures.successfulAnswerRate: completed usable answers divided by attempts
measures.uniqueContributionRate: answers judged to add a non-duplicative useful point divided by completed answers
measures.verificationValue: corrections, fact checks or risk catches that materially change the final answer
measures.disagreementResolutionRate: material model disagreements resolved with a supported conclusion divided by disagreements escalated
measures.truncationRetryRate: calls requiring retry because output was incomplete or unusable
measures.costPerUsefulContribution: actual provider cost divided by accepted useful contributions
measures.costPerSuccessfulRound: total paid cost divided by rounds that produce a materially improved final answer

priorityOrder: restore an otherwise unavailable essential capability
verification or factual challenge when uncertainty is material
resolve meaningful disagreement between independent models
genuinely different reasoning from a provider with proven unique contribution value
speed improvements when quality is unchanged
